candidate.flaw: The forked internal service child serves any HTTP caller on its loopback port; GET /cgi-bin/temp/get?filename= passes a non-temp name straight to a file read, and no route requires the internal uid header until the fix adds a server-wide gate.

verified.exploit_entry_point: Real HTTP requests to the forked internal service component, booted in-process exactly as the product boots it (lib/service/service.js module export -> hagent getServer -> 127.0.0.1:PORT). An unauthenticated GET /cgi-bin/temp/get?filename=<abs path> returns the file's contents; the same holds for a stored-item handle, the ?files= list form, /cgi-bin/saved/list and /cgi-bin/history. Confirmed on the pinned tree in Docker.
sites: lib/service/service.js: server-wide credential gate added in sessionsHandler before the first route (the published fix's out-of-scope-looking lower-level API site)
lib/service/service.js temp/get handler + getTempFiles: stored-handle resolution via the shared helper
lib/util/common.js: getTempFile + WHISTLE_UID_HEADER (shared util; already referenced by biz/webui at the pinned commit, which fixes the contract the gate must honour)

unauth read of a stored item by its 64-hex handle
unauth read via the ?files= batch/list form
unauth access to a non-file internal data route (saved/list)
unauth access to a second non-file route (history)
credential header present but wrong-valued (read outside storage area)

verified.project_tests_run: The project has no existing tests for this area (no test touches temp/get, the list form, isTempFile/getTempFile, the service child, saved/list or history; confirmed by grep across test/). The heavy integration suite (test/index.test.js) is unrelated and not part of the affected area. The in-process boot + loopback-HTTP tests run offline.

traps.name: server-wide credential gate (fix is at the internal server, not the reported endpoint)
traps.shape: lower-level public API / far site: the published fix gates the whole forked internal service, not the file-read endpoint the report points at
traps.where: lib/service/service.js:308-312 (gate inserted in sessionsHandler); reported sink at lib/service/service.js:458-467
traps.reason_to_dismiss: The service child only listens on a random loopback port and is meant to be reached through the web UI, whose proxy already blocks non-temp filenames in no-login mode, so hardening the internal server itself looks out of scope.

traps.realistic_because: The published fix does exactly this (a uid-header gate over the whole service child). A solver who fixes only the reported file-read endpoint leaves every other route of the same unauthenticated server open.

traps.name: authorized full-path read is a deliberate feature (over-broad fix breaks it)
traps.shape: coupled must-keep-working behaviour next to the sink; the obvious hardening (confine the endpoint to the storage directory / block absolute paths) removes a real feature
traps.where: lib/service/service.js:458-467 (getFile receives a raw filename for authorized callers, by design)
traps.reason_to_dismiss: The report describes files being read OUTSIDE the storage area, so the natural fix is to force every read under the storage directory; that an authorized caller may deliberately load a file by full path is not visible from the report's trigger.
coupled_functional_tests: functional/run.js::authorized load of a file by full path works
traps.realistic_because: Loading a local file by absolute path through this endpoint is a deliberate, documented feature for authorized callers; the upstream fix keeps it and only adds authentication. An over-broad confinement fix passes the headline exploit but deletes the feature.

uncovered_routes_not_built.why_real: Registered before the web UI's login middleware, so when login IS configured the no-login guard is skipped and the request is forwarded to the internal service with a valid internal token; the published fix does not touch this file, so it stays open even after the fix (present_in_latest: no; fixed later elsewhere).
uncovered_routes_not_built.why_not_built: Driving it requires standing up the full web UI app wired to a forked service child (proxy plumbing: transformReq/setProxy/pluginMgr). In-process mounting throws (proxyEvent.emit) without reconstructing much of the proxy, which would make the test fragile and no longer a clean drive of product code. Confirmed the route exists and bypasses login by reading the code; not hermetically testable here. Recorded in the register as built=no.

wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: there is a single resource kind (files/stored items served by one component through one credential); no neighbouring or proxy resource can be authorised instead.
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: there are no roles, peers or directions here; the single credential either authorises the caller or it does not.
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the credential check is the first middleware and runs before any normalisation of the attacker-controlled value.
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: the credential is a plain header compared for exact equality to a config value; there is no parsing step whose mismatch could make the guard see nothing.
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: the credential value is generated at process start and is always present; there is no external authority lookup that could return empty and make the guard fail open (the hardening patch additionally fails closed if it were empty).
wrong_fix_catalogue.adjacent_api: n/a: the fix adds a new shared helper and a gate; it does not narrow the contract of any existing shared API that a sibling relies on.

notes: Effectively a pattern-A task: the far/out-of-scope site (the server-wide credential gate) plus a coupled must-keep-working feature with a different reason to dismiss. The specified pattern-B route (import-remote) is a real, unmodified-upstream uncovered route but is not hermetically testable here without reconstructing the proxy; recorded built=no in the register and in uncovered_routes_not_built. Input-shape variants (temp/<hex>, /temp/<hex>, <hex>.<ext>) are NOT testable: on the pinned code those shapes resolve to nothing (neither leak nor work), so they can be neither security nor functional tests.
